title: Conflict of Interest, Explained

endcard.line: Pictures: RandomKatze (CC0); Pearson Scott Foresman (public domain)

anim.title: A case
items: An officer must choose a road contractor
One bidder is her brother's firm
She has done nothing wrong yet

segments.say: An officer has to choose a contractor for a road. One of the bidders is her brother's firm. She hasn't done anything wrong. What should she do?
Her private interest, her brother, now touches her public duty. That is a conflict of interest.

anim.title: What the rules ask
items: Take steps to resolve the conflict

segments.say: India's conduct rules for the All India Services, amended in twenty fourteen, are clear. Declare any private interest that relates to your public duties, and resolve the conflict in a way that protects the public interest.

right.title: Stay silent
items: even a fair choice looks unfair

segments.say: Here, that means telling her seniors and stepping away from the decision. Even if she would have chosen fairly, silence would make the choice look unfair.

anim.title: Related duties in the same rules
items: No obligations that could sway your work
Don't use your position for yourself, family or friends

segments.say: The same rules also say: don't place yourself under obligations that could influence your work, don't use your position to benefit yourself, family or friends, and decide on merit alone.
A conflict of interest is not wrongdoing in itself. Hiding it, or acting on it, is where the harm begins.
For GS Four case studies, follow four steps: name the conflict, declare it, step aside, and let merit decide.

sources: PIB, All India Services (Conduct) Rules, 1968 Amended, 8 August 2014 (relid 108295): new rule 3(1A) (high ethical standards, integrity and honesty; political neutrality; merit, fairness and impartiality; accountability and transparency; responsiveness to the public, particularly weaker sections; courtesy) and rule 3(2B) (uphold the Constitution; decisions solely in public interest; use public resources efficiently; declare any private interests relating to public duties and resolve conflicts in a way that protects the public interest; no financial or other obligations that may influence official duties; not misuse position for benefit of self, family or friends; decide on merit alone; maintain confidentiality as required by law)

quiz.q: Under the 2014 amendment to the All India Services (Conduct) Rules, what must an officer do with a private interest that relates to public duties?
options: Declare it and resolve the conflict in the public interest
quiz.why: Rule 3(2B): declare any private interests and resolve conflicts in a way that protects the public interest.

quiz.q: Which of these is itself a conflict of interest?
options: An officer who disagrees with a policy
An officer deciding a tender a relative has bid for
quiz.why: A private interest touches a public decision.

quiz.q: In the case, what is the best course for the officer?
options: Choose her brother if his bid is lowest
Ask her brother to withdraw quietly
Declare the link and step away from the decision
quiz.why: Declaring and stepping aside keeps the decision on merit and keeps trust.

reviewNote: The rule wording is from PIB's 2014 release on the All India Services (Conduct) Rules; the parallel 2014 change to the CCS (Conduct) Rules wasn't read in full. The case is invented for teaching and names no one. Lines in segments 4 and 6 are reasoning, not sourced facts; an ethics editor should check them. Moving facts: none.
